project.name: Routr
project.title: How much SIP traffic Routr handles.
project.lead: We run these tests after significant changes to the code, on dedicated DigitalOcean servers. Routr runs on one server and on Kubernetes; capacity tests find the limits, then both soak for 2 hours at 70% of them to catch leaks.

narrative.what: The EdgePort on its own, with Echo answering every request with 200 OK.
narrative.why: The EdgePort is the only stateful piece of Routr; this is its ceiling.
narrative.how: SIPp sends SIP MESSAGE over UDP, from 2,000 messages/s, adding 500 every 30 s, up to 30,000.

narrative.what: RoutrOne with the files backend, routing calls between 200 registered Agents. Every call is answered.
narrative.why: How many calls per second one server handles end to end, authentication included.
narrative.how: SIPp registers 200 callees, then ramps authenticated calls held 5 s over UDP, from 100 calls/s, adding 100 every 30 s, up to 6,000.

narrative.what: RoutrOne routing calls between 1,800 registered Agents, 60% answered, 15% busy, 15% cancelled and 10% to offline Agents.
narrative.why: Real traffic is not all answered calls; busy, cancelled and offline calls cost Routr work too.
narrative.how: SIPp registers 1,800 callees, then ramps the mix over UDP, answered calls held 5 s, from 100 calls/s, adding 100 every 30 s, up to 6,000.

benchmarks.title: Routr on Kubernetes, simple calls

narrative.what: The Connect chart on three c-8 nodes, one EdgePort per node behind a DigitalOcean Network Load Balancer, plus three replicas each of Connect and the Data API (Postgres) and two of Location (Redis), each with CPU requests and balanced round robin, routing calls between 200 registered Agents.
narrative.why: How a service-based deployment compares with one server, and what the load balancer costs.
narrative.how: SIPp registers 200 callees through the load balancer, then ramps authenticated calls held 5 s over TCP, from 50 calls/s, adding 50 every 30 s, up to 3,000.

benchmarks.reason: load generator fell behind at 450 calls/s (placed 383.2 calls/s, 85% of offered)

narrative.what: RoutrOne routing the call mix at 70% of the rate the call-mix capacity test reached.
narrative.why: Leaks show only over time; a realistic rate fills memory the way production does.
narrative.how: SIPp holds the mix at 70% of the measured limit, answered calls held 2 minutes, for 2 hours. Memory may grow at most 5 MB/h, failed calls stay under 0.1%, and nothing restarts.

narrative.what: The Connect chart routing simple calls at 70% of the rate its capacity test reached.
narrative.why: Leaks in any service, Redis or Postgres show over time, and pods must not restart.
narrative.how: SIPp holds simple calls at 70% of the measured limit, each held 30 s, for 2 hours. Memory may grow at most 5 MB/h per component, failed calls stay under 0.1%, and no pod restarts.
